matchstick.title: Preserve stick orientation
matchstick.principle: When moving a matchstick, keep its original orientation (vertical, horizontal, or diagonal); you cannot rotate a stick.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Any time you relocate a stick, verify that the new placement uses the same orientation as the original.
matchstick.example: Moving a diagonal stick from a V and placing it as a vertical line, which creates an invalid I.

matchstick.title: No addition or removal of sticks
matchstick.principle: Exactly one existing stick may be moved; you cannot create a new stick or discard a stick without placing it elsewhere.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Before finalizing a transformation, ensure the total number of sticks remains unchanged and only one stick is relocated.
matchstick.example: Removing a stick from the equals sign and not placing it elsewhere, leaving only one horizontal line.

matchstick.title: Maintain valid characters
matchstick.principle: After moving a stick, every token must still be a legal Roman numeral (I, V, X, L, C, D, M) or a recognized operator (+, -, =).
matchstick.when_to_apply: After the move, check each token's shape against the set of allowed characters.
matchstick.example: Leaving a single diagonal stick after taking one away from a V, which is not a valid numeral.

matchstick.title: Verify arithmetic correctness
matchstick.principle: Convert the Roman numerals on both sides of the equation to Arabic numbers and ensure the equality holds after the move.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After you think the transformation is valid, compute the numeric values to confirm the equation is true.
matchstick.example: Accepting an equation that is syntactically valid but numerically false, such as 'XV = XVI - XV' (15 ≠ 1).

matchstick.title: Answer formatting
matchstick.principle: The final response must end with a line exactly matching ‘Correct version of the equation: <equation>’, with uppercase letters and collapsed whitespace.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When writing the final answer, ensure the line follows the exact required format.
matchstick.example: Writing ‘Correct version of the equation:XVIII = XII + VI’ without the required space after the colon.

matchstick.title: Preserve exactly one equals sign
matchstick.principle: The equation must contain exactly one ‘=’ operator after the move; you cannot remove it, add another, or change it into a different symbol.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When considering moving sticks from the equals sign, avoid doing so; keep both horizontal sticks intact.
matchstick.example: Removing a horizontal stick from ‘=’, turning it into ‘-’, which violates the rule of having exactly one equals sign.

matchstick.title: Preserve operator integrity
matchstick.principle: When moving a stick that belongs to an operator (+ or -), ensure the remaining sticks still form a recognized operator; e.g., removing the vertical from ‘+’ yields ‘-’, which is only allowed if the operator is intended to become ‘-’.
matchstick.when_to_apply: If you consider taking a stick from a plus or minus sign, verify the resulting shape is still a valid operator.
matchstick.example: Taking the vertical stick from ‘+’ and not adding a horizontal, leaving a lone horizontal line that is not a recognized operator.

matchstick.title: Token preservation
matchstick.principle: After moving a stick, each original token (numeral or operator) must still be present in the equation; you cannot merge two tokens or split one into two.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After the move, count the tokens and ensure the same number of numerals and operators appear as before.
matchstick.example: Changing ‘XV’ to ‘I’ by removing both the X and V sticks, effectively deleting a token.

matchstick.title: Single-stick move verification
matchstick.principle: Ensure the transformation can be achieved by moving exactly one stick; only one token's stick count may change, and no other token should be altered beyond the moved stick.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Before finalizing, verify that only one stick was moved and that no other token was implicitly changed.
matchstick.example: Changing ‘XV’ to ‘XVI’ by adding a stick to create the I, which requires adding a stick rather than moving only one.

matchstick.title: Intra-token stick relocation
matchstick.principle: You may relocate a stick within the same numeral to change its shape, preserving orientation, as long as the resulting shape is a valid numeral; this can adjust the numeral's value without affecting other tokens.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the needed numeric adjustment matches the value change achievable by repositioning a stick inside a numeral (e.g., turning V into X by crossing its diagonals).
matchstick.example: Trying to turn V into X by moving a stick from another token, instead of simply repositioning one diagonal within the V itself.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model focuses on the visual transformation and neglects to check whether the resulting Roman numerals satisfy the equality.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After proposing a transformation, convert both sides to Arabic numbers and confirm the equality before finalizing the answer.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model generates the final line without adhering to the exact required syntax, such as missing spaces or using wrong capitalization.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Always end the response with the line ‘Correct version of the equation: <equation>’, ensuring uppercase letters and a single space after the colon.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model removes a stick from a token but does not place it elsewhere, effectively deleting a stick.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: When moving a stick, immediately decide its new location and ensure it is placed on another token, preserving the total stick count.

matchstick.description: Invalid operator after moving a stick
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model moves a stick from a plus or minus sign without ensuring the remaining sticks still form a recognized operator.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: If you take a stick from an operator, verify that the resulting shape is still a valid operator (+, -, =) or avoid moving sticks from operators altogether.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model treats the equals sign like any other operator and attempts to move a stick from it to adjust numerals, forgetting the rule that exactly one '=' must remain unchanged.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Never move sticks from the equals sign; keep both horizontal sticks intact, and obtain any needed stick from a numeral or other operator instead.
